decision_conditions: The proposed development constitutes inappropriate development within the Green Belt, which is harmful by definition. The scheme does not fall within any of the exceptions identified in paragraph 154 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), and while the site may be considered Grey Belt, the proposal fails to satisfy the appropriateness tests set out in paragraph 155(b) and (c), relating to unmet need and sustainable location. No very special circumstances have been demonstrated that would clearly outweigh this harm. The proposal is therefore contrary to paragraphs 154 and 155 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One - Strategic Policies (2012), and Policies DMH 6 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development would not be classed as "limited infilling in a village" as set out under paragraph 154 (e) of the NPPF. The site is a large open field and the development of six dwellings would not equate to the filling of a small gap in an otherwise built-up frontage.The established character of Springwell Lane is defined by detached and semi-detached dwellings arranged in linear plots with long gardens, supported by the verdant and undeveloped qualities of the application site which contribute positively to the village setting. Introducing six dwellings would erode the openness of the Green Belt  and fail to be sympathetic to the prevailing character, grain and landscaping setting of the village.  The proposal therefore conflicts with paragraphs 154(e) and 135(c) of the NPPF and with relevant design and Green Belt policies of the Development Plan.

The site is not an appropriate location for residential development. The proposed quantum of up to six dwellings, would represent an inappropriate intensification of the site. The courtyard cluster would appear out of keeping with the spacious, linear grain of development. In addition, the site performs poorly in accessibility terms: it is located on the northern edge of Harefield with a PTAL rating of 0, no footway access, and a reliance on private car use reinforced by the proposed on-site parking provision. The location is therefore unsuitable and unsustainable for new housing, contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021), Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies DMHB 11 and Policy DMHB 17 of the Local Plan Part Two (2020) and paragraphs 110 and 115 of the NPPF (2024
